historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (3.1%) and FY27 guidance midpoint (+2.2%), lifted slightly for the FY24-26 underlying run-rate of 6.4%/yr that management attributes two-thirds to price increases
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-1.7% 3yr, -18.4% 5yr) and unusable: FY23 carried a ~$281m goodwill impairment and FY25 a $73.2m return of capital. EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY23 EPS -$0.917); 5yr uses FY26 UNDERLYING EPS 14.2c (reported 25.0c includes the $47.8m DTA credit) against FY21 13.9c. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR undefined (FY23 owner FCF -$9.9m); the 5yr figure of 14.8% (FY21 $39.1m -> FY26 $78.1m, reported FCF less SBC less interest income, leases not deducted in the older years because principal repayments were not extracted) describes a cost-out recovery, not a growth rate, and is not used for projection.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on revenue from contracts with customers (Metrics.csv): FY23 $248.2m -> FY26 $282.6m; FY21 $242.3m -> FY26 $282.6m. FY25's $313.0m includes the $56.2m Fidelity licence and is skipped as an endpoint. Owner-FCF CAGR (14.8%) far exceeds the revenue CAGR because FY21-26 was a margin recovery from a loss-making base; SBC is not a factor (0.2-0.9% of revenue throughout).

scenario_narratives.base: Bravura is a mission-critical registry and wealth-administration software vendor whose reported history is a restructuring, not a cycle: FY23 impairment, FY25 Fidelity licence windfall, FY26 DTA credit. The base case starts from FY26 UNDERLYING (revenue $283.6m, Cash EBITDA $77.1m, NPAT $63.1m), takes FY27 at the guidance midpoint (revenue $290m, Cash EBITDA ~$88m), grows 3-4%/yr on CPI-plus contract escalation and Sonata Alta / Midwinter upsell, and lets EBITDA reach 35% by FY29 (segments already run 45-48%). The single most important normalisation is the cash tax rate: 13% today on loss utilisation, 27% blended statutory by FY32. Year-1 owner FCF of ~$77m (26% margin) reconciles to guidance less ~$11m cash tax; terminal-year owner FCF margin ~23.5% after full tax.
scenario_narratives.bull: New logos and Midwinter digital-advice seats replace churn, Sonata Alta modules upsell into the installed base, revenue compounds 6% through FY30 and EBITDA reaches 39%. The AIM listing broadens the register and the $100m facility funds bolt-ons that are not in these numbers. Consolidator interest (FNZ bought GBST in 2025 after a contested process in which Bravura bid) is the unmodelled kicker.
scenario_narratives.bear: Client concentration bites: another large client leaves for FNZ/SS&C, GBP/AUD translation turns against reported results, and with price increases exhausted revenue stalls at $280m before creeping at 2%. Margin drifts back to 30% as the cost-out is complete and a new CEO/CFO have to reinvest in delivery. The business stays cash-generative and net cash -- the downside is a de-rating to an ex-growth multiple, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the underlying, not the reported. Bravura's last four years of reported earnings are dominated by one-offs of both signs (a $281m impairment, a $56m licence sale, a $48m tax credit) and by a cost-out that has now largely run; the model therefore anchors on FY26 underlying revenue, EBITDA and cash tax, reproduces management's Cash EBITDA definition from components, and normalises the two things the reported numbers would otherwise perpetuate -- the loss-sheltered cash tax rate and FY26's working-capital inflow. SBC is expensed (it is tiny; incentives are paid in cash and on-market-purchased shares) and the count is held flat. Leases are an operating cost and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Risk is charged in the bear driver path and its 25% weight, not by inflating the 10% AUD WACC. The house value should be read against the price as a required-return question: the required_return_table shows what today's $3.26 implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Client concentration: loss of one more large client after two exits in FY26 -- the bear axis; the model has no visibility on individual contract renewal dates
Growth quality: two-thirds of FY26 organic growth was price increases on the installed base; if pricing power is exhausted the base case's 3-4% growth is too high

Cash tax normalisation: the model assumes the loss shelter is used up in ~4 years; if the $88m of unrecognised losses proves larger or more usable the near-term flows are understated, if UK/AU rates rise the terminal rate is understated
FX translation: ~72% of revenue is GBP; a 10% GBP/AUD move shifts AUD revenue ~7% with a smaller effect on AUD EBITDA because costs are also GBP-heavy
Leadership transition: new CEO (Jan 2026) and CFO departure during the turnaround; the FY23 delivery failures show what execution slippage costs
Capital allocation: the $50m buyback at ~$3.1-3.6 is above the house base IV, and the $100m facility signals M&A appetite; bolt-ons at software multiples would be dilutive to value at these prices
Unmodelled upside: strategic take-out by FNZ/SS&C at a control premium -- the reason the market may pay more than the standalone DCF

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, BVS.AX, 2026-09-22T05:14:28Z regular session; ex-dividend 2026-08-24 ($0.15) confirmed from the same endpoint's dividend events
data_sources.financials: BVS.AX_Metrics.csv (rebuilt from core_metrics 2026-09-22) for the history; BVS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt for FY26 P&L (lines 539-570), balance sheet (1735-1765), cash flow (1838-1894), Cash EBITDA reconciliation (2715-2730), tax note 7 (2985-3032), EPS note 8 (3050-3074), share capital note 16 (3470-3504), shareholder information (4396-4401)
data_sources.qualitative: BVS.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-22): business model, competitive position, FY27 guidance (revenue $280-300m, Cash EBITDA $84-94m, ~65% pre-contracted), bull/bear cases, recent developments (AIM admission 28 Jul 2026, $100m facility 7 Aug 2026, $50m buyback 12 Aug 2026)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY26 underlying group revenue per the FY26 Annual Report OFR (BVS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:544): $282.553m revenue from contracts with customers (the Metrics.csv figure) plus $1.1m other income (R&D incentives). This is the basis on which the company states EBITDA margin and on which FY27 guidance ($280-300m) is framed, so the margin path compounds from it.
inputs.share_count_basis: 448,299,975 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (note 16a, BVS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3486). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The count INCLUDES the 7,833,073 shares held by the Employee Share Trust (note 16b, line 3504): those were bought on-market ($16.7m in FY26) specifically to settle granted-but-unvested employee awards, so they will be delivered to employees and are economically outstanding. The 440,466,902 'held by shareholders' figure at 6 Aug 2026 (line 4400) excludes them and would understate the diluted count. Diluted EPS note (line 3071) confirms no other dilutive instruments. The $50m on-market buyback announced 12 Aug 2026 had not executed at 6 Aug and is value-neutral in this model (section 1 of owner-fcf.md).
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings nil at 30 June 2026; cash and equivalents $50.296m (balance sheet, BVS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt). Lease liabilities of $6.936m ($2.691m current + $4.245m non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt because leases are charged as an operating cost inside the flows (treatment B). The $100m committed debt facility (7 Aug 2026) was undrawn at balance date and is not in the bridge. The FY26 final + special dividend of $67.3m, declared after balance date and unpaid at 30 June, is deducted in equity_bridge because the price is already ex-dividend (ex-date 2026-08-24).

owner_fcf_bridge.note: last_fcf deducts two items beyond the standard sbc + interest_income identity: cash lease payments ($3.159m ROU principal + $0.391m lease interest, both on the FY26 cash-flow statement, lines 1875-1877) under lease treatment B, and $0.585m of capitalised software development (line 1867) which the CSV's FCF definition (OCF less PPE capex) omits. FY26 owner FCF also carries roughly $10-14m of working-capital inflow (accrued bonuses +$6.4m, contract-asset unwind) that the component build does not carry forward; FY26 Cash EBITDA of $77.1m less $9.4m cash tax is the cleaner ~$68m run-rate.

inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report, statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payments' $720k (BVS.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:1802) and cash-flow reconciliation (line 2934, $732k). Equity-award taxes: nil disclosed (KPI EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). SBC is tiny because the FY26/FY27 incentive plans are settled in cash and in shares bought on-market with employees' after-tax bonus proceeds (remuneration report, line 1452) -- that cost already sits in employee benefits expense inside EBITDA, so it is not double-counted here.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY26 'On-market share buyback' financing outflow was nil; the $16.715m is 'Purchases of equity by Employee Share Trust' (cash-flow statement line 1883), which is the cash mechanism by which the count is held flat against employee awards. The $50m on-market buyback (announced 12 Aug 2026, non-adjusting event, line 830) is authorised, not spent, at the balance-sheet date.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote both AUD; no conversion. Roughly 72% of revenue and a similar share of costs are GBP-denominated (EMEA segment), so the AUD flows carry GBP/AUD translation exposure -- that is a driver-path risk (bear case), not a currency-mismatch in the model. The AIM depositary-interest line (July 2026) is a secondary quote in GBp and is not used here.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T05:14:28Z (ASX intraday, regular session; Yahoo regularMarketTime). Ex-dividend since 2026-08-24 ($0.15 final + special).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: 10-year ACGB ~4.4% risk-free, 5.5% equity risk premium, beta ~1.1 for an ASX small-cap enterprise-software vendor with 55% recurring revenue but a turnaround history -> cost of equity ~10.5%; no drawn debt, so WACC = 10.0% rounded (a small allowance for the undrawn $100m facility being used). The same 10.0% is applied to all three scenarios: client-concentration, churn, FX and leadership-transition risk are charged in the bear driver path and its 25% weight, not in the discount rate (section 7f, charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path charges the full cash lease payment (principal + interest = $3.55m, 1.25% of revenue in FY26) inside adjusted EBITDA; lease liabilities ($6.9m) are excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation ($8.646m per the OFR, line 559, vs $13.871m total on the P&L face) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no non-controlling interests; net profit is wholly attributable to members.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component-built, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping through FY29), scenario-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating enterprise-software company (wealth/superannuation registry and digital-advice software), no prior valuation, no memory entry. NORMALISATION JUDGMENT: the reported history is unusable as a base -- FY23 NPAT -$280.7m (goodwill impairment), FY25 revenue/EBITDA/OCF include the one-off $56.2m Fidelity perpetual-licence sale, FY26 NPAT $110.9m includes a $47.8m non-cash deferred-tax-asset recognition. Rather than a mid-cycle average (there is no cycle here, only a restructuring followed by a cost-out), the base year is FY26 UNDERLYING: revenue $283.6m, EBITDA $84.7m (29.9%), Cash EBITDA $77.1m (27.2%), underlying NPAT $63.1m, cash tax paid $9.4m. Every forward line is built from components anchored to those underlying figures and to FY27 guidance (revenue $280-300m, Cash EBITDA $84-94m, ~65% pre-contracted), NOT carried forward from reported FY26 FCF. The two silent overstatements this avoids: (1) the FY26 cash tax rate (~13% of PBT) is a loss-shelter artefact -- $11.7m/yr of unbooked losses were utilised in each of FY25 and FY26, and the remaining shelter (DTA on losses $22.5m tax-effected plus $88.1m of still-unrecognised losses, note 7) is exhausted in roughly four years, so cash_tax_rate_path ramps 13% -> 27% (blend of UK 25% on ~72% of profit and Australia 30%, plus withholding) by FY32; (2) FY26 owner FCF of $74m carries a working-capital inflow that is not repeatable. Cash EBITDA as the company defines it (EBITDA less development costs, capex and lease costs) is reproduced in the build as EBITDA less lease_cost_pct less capex_pct: FY27 base EBITDA 33.0% of $290.7m = $95.9m less lease $3.6m less capex $4.4m = $87.9m, inside the $84-94m guidance range. The Analysis JSON's statement that the shares 'fell to just over $2' on results day is inconsistent with Yahoo closes ($3.14 on 12 Aug, $3.59 on 14 Aug, $3.15 by 24 Aug); the $2.02 figure is the 30 June 2026 close in the remuneration report's five-year table. Not relied on.

bear.narrative: FY27 at the bottom of guidance ($280m, -1%) as a further large client migrates to FNZ/SS&C and GBP weakens against AUD; price-increase-led growth is exhausted (management: two-thirds of FY26 organic growth was price) and revenue only tracks CPI from FY29. Margin slips back toward 30% as cost-out is finished and delivery capacity has to be rebuilt under a new CEO and incoming CFO. Cash tax ramps identically. Terminal 2.0%, cap 12x. Not a solvency case: net cash, no drawn debt, and the flows stay positive throughout -- the bear here is an ex-growth registry vendor at a mid-teens FCF multiple.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 at the guidance midpoint ($290m, +2.2%; rounded to 2.5% on the 283.6 base). FY28-29 at 4% as Sonata Alta migrations and Midwinter digital-advice seats add to CPI-plus price escalation, then a glide to 2.5% terminal. History supports no more: 3.1% 5yr revenue CAGR, and management concedes two-thirds of FY26 organic growth was price.
base.margin_rationale: IFRS-16 EBITDA (pre-lease, pre-SBC) was 29.9% in FY26. FY27 guidance Cash EBITDA $84-94m implies ~33% EBITDA at the midpoint once lease ($3.6m) and capex ($4.4m) are added back. Segment margins are already 47.5% EMEA / 44.8% APAC against $47.9m of unallocated cost (17% of revenue); a further 2pp of group margin from cost-out and AI-assisted delivery takes it to 35% by FY29 and holds -- around SS&C/Temenos levels, below best-in-class SaaS.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax as % of EBIT ramps 13% -> 27%. FY26 current tax was $10.2m on $74.9m PBT because $11.7m of unbooked losses were utilised; the recognised DTA on losses ($22.5m) plus $88.1m of unrecognised losses shelter roughly four more years at that pace, after which the blended statutory rate (UK 25% x ~72%, AU 30% x ~28%, plus ~1pp withholding) applies. Deductible temporary differences ($26.9m recognised) reverse more slowly and are inside the ramp.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A ex-ROU $8.6m (3.0%) is inflated by amortisation of acquired intangibles ($28.2m carrying value) that will not be replaced; it converges to the 1.5% capex run-rate (PPE $3.6m + capitalised software $0.6m = $4.2m in FY26; hosting-asset depreciation of $2.3m is already inside EBITDA) by FY32 so the terminal tax shield is not overstated.
base.wc_rationale: 5% capture on the revenue change: contract liabilities ($25.3m) are ~9% of revenue but contract assets and accrued bonuses move the other way; FY26's ~$12m inflow was bonus-accrual timing and is not carried forward.

bull.narrative: FY27 at the top of guidance ($295m) with new-logo wins (Midwinter now at 6m+ members; Payday Super and UK Consumer Duty project work) replacing FY26 churn; 6%/yr through FY30 as Sonata Alta modular upsell lands; EBITDA to 39% as unallocated cost keeps falling and AI-assisted delivery lifts services margin. Tax ramp unchanged -- the loss shelter is exhausted faster on higher profits, so it is not a bull lever. Terminal 3.0%, cap 18x. Strategic take-out by FNZ or SS&C is NOT modelled -- it is optionality on top of this case.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: the company itself discloses dependence on 'a relatively small number of significant clients', two large clients exited in FY26, two-thirds of FY26 organic growth was pricing, and both the CEO (Jan 2026) and CFO (search underway) are new. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs new-logo growth AND a further 6pp of margin AND favourable FX to all land, while the most plausible bull outcome -- a strategic take-out by FNZ or SS&C -- is not in the DCF at all. Base 50%: FY27 guidance is ~65% pre-contracted and the margin recovery is already banked in FY26 underlying numbers.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapsed: SBC is 0.25% of revenue (FY26 $0.72m), so house and street IVs differ by ~$0.02 and band_position is not meaningful. Reported as null per owner-fcf.md section 7(e); the incentive cost sits in cash employee expenses inside EBITDA.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
